rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The sons are told to enter Egypt through different gates; the first phrase means one of the city's gates.
rows.anchor: يعني من باب واحد من أبوابها . { وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة } , قاله الجمهور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The warning can instead mean that they should not take one route into Egypt, but use separate routes.
rows.anchor: من طريق واحد من طرقها { وادخلوا من أبواب متفرقة } أي طرق , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Jacob feared the evil eye because his sons were handsome and striking in appearance.
rows.anchor: أنه خاف عليهم العين لأنهم كانوا ذوي صور وجمال , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
rows.claim: Another view is that the king might see their numbers and strength and attack them from envy or apprehension.
rows.anchor: أن يرى عددهم وقوتهم فيبطش بهم حسدا أو حذرا , قاله بعض المتأخرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob gives practical advice about what he fears, then entrusts the outcome to God because no precaution can independently avail them.
rows.anchor: فأشار عليهم في الأول , وفوض إلى الله في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human caution cannot turn aside God's decree.
rows.anchor: أي لا يرد حذر المخلوق قضاء الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The need in Jacob's heart was a compassionate fear, calmed by his instruction that his sons disperse because of the evil eye.
rows.anchor: حذر المشفق وسكون نفس بالوصية أن يتفرقوا خشية العين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Being learned from what God taught means that Jacob acted on his knowledge.
rows.anchor: إنه لعامل بما علم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Jacob was certain of God's promise.
rows.anchor: لمتيقن بوعدنا , وهو معنى قول الضحاك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that Jacob faithfully guarded God's instruction.
rows.anchor: إنه لحافظ لوصيتنا , وهو معنى قول الكلبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Joseph drew his brother close, embraced him, and lodged him with himself.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : ضمه إليه وأنزله معه

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Joseph disclosed that he was the brother Yusuf.
rows.anchor: أنه أخبره أنه يوسف أخوه , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Alternatively, he said he would be the brother's brother in place of the brother who had died.
rows.anchor: أنا أخوك مكان أخيك الهالك , قاله وهب

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: The reassurance means not to grieve; the phrase is also glossed simply as not to be sad.
rows.anchor: فلا تأسف , قاله ابن بحر . الثاني : فلا تحزن بما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the brothers had done may refer to their past treatment of Benjamin and Joseph.
rows.anchor: بما فعلوه في الماضي بك وبأخيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the brothers' monopolizing their father's wealth while excluding Benjamin.
rows.anchor: باستبدادهم دونك بمال أبيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph measured out their food after honoring them and gave Benjamin a camel-load like the others received.
rows.anchor: وهو كيل الطعام لهم بعد إكرامهم وإعطائه بعيرا لأخيهم مثل ما أعطاهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The drinking vessel and the king's bowl are one object; a suwaʿ is any vessel used for drinking.
rows.anchor: والسقاية والصواع واحد . قال ابن عباس . وكل شيء يشرب فيه فهو صواع

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A cited poem uses suwaʿ for a vessel from which wine is drunk.
rows.anchor: نشرب الخمر بالصواع جهارا وترى المتك بيننا مستعارا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The vessel was the cup used to drink mutak.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : وكان إناء المتك الذي يشرب فيه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: One account says the vessel was made of silver.
rows.anchor: فقال عكرمة كان من فضة

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: Another account says it was gold, and that food was measured with it as an added honor.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : كان من ذهب , وبه كال طعامهم مبالغة في إكرامهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies it as an ordinary mukuk whose two ends meet.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي : هو المكوك العادي الذي يلتقي طرفاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is called an adhan because it announces something, just as the call to prayer does.
rows.anchor: فسمى النداء أذانا لأنه إعلام كالأذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayr can mean the traveling caravan.
rows.anchor: وفي { العير } وجهان : أحدهما : أنها الرفقة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-ayr can instead mean the loaded camels used for riding.
rows.anchor: أنها الإبل المرحولة المركوبة , قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One defense is that the measurer who hid the vessel did so without Joseph's order.
rows.anchor: أنها معصية فعلها الكيال ولم يأمر بها يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another defense is that the caller suspected the brothers of theft without knowing Joseph had arranged the placement.
rows.anchor: ظن أنهم سرقوها ولم يعلم بما فعله يوسف , فلم يكن عاصيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third defense says Joseph ordered the announcement but meant that the brothers had stolen Joseph from his father, which was true.
rows.anchor: وعنى بذلك سرقتهم ليوسف من أبيه , وذلك صدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth view treats Joseph's act as a fault for which God let the brothers accuse him of earlier theft.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت خطيئة من قبل يوسف فعاقبه الله عليها

rows.speaker: بعض من يقول بغوامض المعاني
rows.claim: An esoteric interpretation takes “you are thieves” to mean they had wronged their father by taking and betraying their brother.
rows.anchor: أي لعاقون لأبيكم في أمر أخيكم حيث أخذتموه منه وخنتموه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers ask what is missing in startled disbelief, confident of their own innocence.
rows.anchor: لأنهم استنكروا ما قذفوا به مع ثقتهم بأنفسهم فاستفهموا استفهام المبهوت

rows.speaker: غالب الليثي عن يحيى بن يعمر
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar is reported to read suwaʿ with ghayn, relating it to something fashioned from silver, gold, or copper.
rows.anchor: وحكى غالب الليثي عن يحيى بن يعمر أنه كان يقرأ صوغ الملك بالغين معجمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised camel-load is a reward or finder's fee offered to whoever brings the vessel.
rows.anchor: وهذه جعالة بذلت للواجد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The load is the amount carried by a camel.
rows.anchor: حمل جمل , وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In a dialect, the load can mean the amount carried by a donkey.
rows.anchor: حمل حمار , وهو لغة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller may have offered the reward personally, since he says he guarantees it.
rows.anchor: أن المنادي بذله عن نفسه لأنه قال { وأنا به زعيم } أي كفيل ضامن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer to the uncertainty objection is that a camel-load was a familiar, known measure, so guaranteeing it was valid.
rows.anchor: أن حمل البعير قد كان عندهم معلوما كالسوق فصح ضمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that finder's fees allow uncertainty and a guarantee of something not otherwise owed.
rows.anchor: أنها جعالة وقد أجاز بعض الفقهاء فيها في الجهالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial that they came to spread corruption means they came to steal, since theft is corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: ما جئنا لنفسد في الأرض } أي لنسرق , لأن السرقة من الفساد في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say this because the Egyptians already knew them for righteousness and chastity.
rows.anchor: لأنهم قد كانوا عرفوهم بالصلاح والعفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another supporting argument is that they returned the goods found in their packs; someone who returns lost property would not steal present property.
rows.anchor: لأنهم ردوا البضاعة التي وجدوها في رحالهم , ومن يؤد الأمانة في غائب لا يقدم على سرقة مال حاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible meaning is that they had never stolen from anyone besides these people, so would not steal from them.
rows.anchor: ما كنا سارقين من غيركم فنسرق منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The more fitting meaning is that they do not betray your trust and then steal your property, because it speaks to their established conduct.
rows.anchor: وهذا أشبه لأنهم أضافوا بذلك إلى عملهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask what penalty should apply to a thief if the brothers are lying about not stealing from them.
rows.anchor: أي ما عقوبة من سرق منكم إن كنتم كاذبين في أنكم لم تسرقوا منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer means that the person found with the stolen property is enslaved; this was Jacob's law for punishing thieves.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء من سرق إن يسترق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph searched their containers before Benjamin's so that the brothers would not suspect a setup if his was searched first.
rows.anchor: لتزول الريبة من قلوبهم لو بدىء بوعاء أخيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun may refer to the drinking vessel; alternatively it refers to suwaʿ, which can be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: قيل عنى السقاية فلذلك أنث , وقيل عنى الصاع , وهو يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The phrase “We contrived for Joseph” can mean that God made or worked things for him.
rows.anchor: صنعنا ليوسف قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: It can also mean that God planned or devised a way for Joseph.
rows.anchor: دبرنا ليوسف , قاله ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The king's “religion” here means his authority or rule.
rows.anchor: في سلطان الملك , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another explanation is that “religion” means the king's judgment or legal system.
rows.anchor: في قضاء الملك , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: A third explanation is the king's custom; his law did not enslave a thief.
rows.anchor: في عادة الملك , قال ابن عيسى : ولم يكن في دين الملك استرقاق من سرق

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Under the king's law a thief instead had to pay a doubled amount.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك : وإنما كان يضاعف عليه الغرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception can mean that God willed the thief to be enslaved.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يشاء الله أن يسترق من سرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God willed to provide Joseph an excuse for what he did.
rows.anchor: أن يجعل ليوسف عذرا فيما فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' statement that a brother had stolen before refers to Joseph.
rows.anchor: يعنون يوسف

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: One explanation is that God punished Joseph by putting this accusation on his brothers' tongues.
rows.anchor: أنه عقوبة ليوسف أجراها الله تعالى على ألسنتهم , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they distanced themselves from Benjamin's act, saying he was not their mother's child and inherited a thief's disposition from Joseph.
rows.anchor: ليتبرأوا بذلك من فعله لأنه ليس من أمهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وقتادة
rows.claim: One report says Joseph stole a silver-and-gold idol belonging to his maternal grandfather, broke it, and discarded it in the road.
rows.anchor: أنه سرق صنما كان لجده إلى أمه من فضة وذهب , وكسره وألقاه في الطريق

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: Another says Joseph hid a piece of meat while eating with his siblings.
rows.anchor: كان مع إخوته على طعام فنظر إلى عرق فخبأه

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: A third account says he took food from the table to give to the poor.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يسرق من طعام المائدة للمساكين , حكاه ابن عيسى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A fourth account says Joseph's aunt hid Isaac's belt on him so she could retain him; she had fostered him and was intensely attached to him.
rows.anchor: فلما أراد يعقوب أخذه منها جعلت المنطقة , واتهمته فأخذتها منه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A fifth view is that the brothers simply lied about Joseph stealing.
rows.anchor: أنهم كذبوا عليه فيما نسبوه إليه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة وعلي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Joseph kept their words about a brother stealing inside himself.
rows.anchor: أنه أسر في نفسه قولهم { إن يسرق فقد سرق أخ له من قبل }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Alternatively, he kept his reply, “You are worse,” inside himself.
rows.anchor: أسر في نفسه { أنتم شر مكانا . . . } الآية , قاله ابن عباس وابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Worse in place” can mean that they had a worse standing before God than the person they accused.
rows.anchor: أنتم شر منزلة عند الله ممن نسبتموه إلى هذه السرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they were worse in conduct because they wronged their brother and disobeyed their father.
rows.anchor: شر صنعا لما أقدمتم عليه من ظلم أخيكم وعقوق أبيكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “God knows what you describe” can mean God knows what you say.
rows.anchor: بما تقولون , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: It can instead mean God knows that they are lying.
rows.anchor: بما تكذبون , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: A story says Joseph tapped the cup, which revealed the brothers' number and that they had sold Joseph; Benjamin then asked whether Joseph was alive, and the cup said he was.
rows.anchor: وحكى بعض المفسرين أنهم لما دخلوا عليه دعا بالصواع فنقره

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: In the same story, Benjamin asked the cup to expose the theft; it replied that it was angry because it had seen its owner with the thief.
rows.anchor: افقر صواعك ليخبرك بالذي سرقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers call their father old and elderly to soften Joseph and elicit sympathy.
rows.anchor: لكن قالوا ذلك ترقيقا واستعطافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Great” may describe their father's advanced age.
rows.anchor: كبير السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead mean great in rank, since his age is already evident from calling him a sheikh.
rows.anchor: كبير القدر لأن كبر السن معروف من حال الشيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their request to take one of them in Benjamin's place means to take him as a substitute slave.
rows.anchor: أي عبدا بدله

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: “We see you as a benefactor” may mean they regard Joseph as beneficent if he grants this request.
rows.anchor: نراك من المحسنين في هذا إن فعلت , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they refer to Joseph's earlier generosity in honoring them, giving them their full measure, and returning their goods.
rows.anchor: فيما كنت تفعله بنا من إكرامنا وتوفية كيلنا وبضاعتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible meaning is that Joseph is fair, since a just person is a benefactor.
rows.anchor: إنا نراك من العادلين , لأن العادل محسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph refuses to take an innocent person in place of the one found with their property, which would be unjust.
rows.anchor: إن أخذنا بريئا بسقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he would be unjust in their eyes if he judged them by a rule other than their father's law that a thief is enslaved.
rows.anchor: إذا حكمنا عليكم بغير حكم أبيكم أن من سرق استرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They despaired of him” means they lost hope that Joseph would return their brother.
rows.anchor: أي يئسوا من رد أخيهم عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Alternatively, they became certain that he would not return Benjamin; a cited line uses the verb in this sense.
rows.anchor: استيقنوا أنه لا يرد عليهم , قاله أبو عبيدة وأنشد قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They withdrew to confer privately, away from the others.
rows.anchor: خلا بعضهم ببعض يتناجون ويتشاورون لا يختلط بهم غيرهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One identification of the eldest is Shimon, foremost in intelligence and learning, who had kept Joseph as hostage when the brothers returned.
rows.anchor: كبيرهم في العقل والعلم وهو شمعون الذي كان قد ارتهن يوسف عنده

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another identification is Reuben, eldest in age and Joseph's cousin through his maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: كبيرهم في السن وهو روبيل ابن خالة يوسف , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A third identification is Judah, eldest in judgment and discernment.
rows.anchor: كبيرهم في الرأي والتمييز وهو يهوذا , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge from God was taken from the brothers when their father sent this son with them.
rows.anchor: يعني عند إيفاد ابنه هذا معكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their earlier failure concerning Joseph means that they had neglected and lost him.
rows.anchor: أي ضيعتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The eldest will stay in Egypt until his father permits him to return.
rows.anchor: يعني أرض مصر . { حتى يأذن لي أبي

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: “Or God judges for me” means that God decrees that he may leave Egypt.
rows.anchor: أو يقضي الله لي بالخروج منها , وهو قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: It may instead mean that God rules in his favor through fighting, since the brothers contemplated doing so.
rows.anchor: أو يحكم الله لي بالسيف والمحاربة لأنهم هموا بذلك , قاله أبو صالح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read the word for “stole” with a damma on sin, kasra on ra, and a doubled ra, making it an accusation of theft.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس { سرق } بضم السين وكسر الراء وتشديدها

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: “We testified only to what we knew” may mean they told their father his son stole because they found the vessel in his pack.
rows.anchor: بأن ابنك سرق إلا بما علمنا من وجود السرقة في رحله , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Alternatively, they told Joseph that a thief is enslaved because they knew that was Jacob's law.
rows.anchor: بأن السارق يسترق إلا بما علمنا من دينك , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: “We could not guard the unseen” means they did not know Benjamin would steal.
rows.anchor: ما كنا نعلم أن ابنك يسرق , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: It may instead mean they did not know that Benjamin would be enslaved.
rows.anchor: ما كنا نعلم أن ابنك يسترق , وهو قول مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The town they ask Jacob to question is Egypt; “its people” is omitted concisely because context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: وهي مصر , والمعنى واسأل أهل القرية فحذف ذكر الأهل إيجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ayr means the caravan, with a camel caravan named by analogy.
rows.anchor: أنها القافلة , وقافلة الإبل تسمى عيرا على التشبيه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-ayr may also mean donkeys, with their people intended.
rows.anchor: الحمير , قاله مجاهد , والمعنى أهل العير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view has Jacob question the town itself or the caravan animals as a prophetic miracle enabling inanimate things and animals to testify.
rows.anchor: أو نفس العير وإن كانت حيوانا بهيما لأنه نبي , والأنبياء قد سخر لهم الجماد والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By calling the town and caravan as witnesses, the brothers offer proof that they are telling the truth about Benjamin's theft.
rows.anchor: أي يستشهدون بصدقنا أن ابنك سرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your souls made it easy” can mean they facilitated the matter.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : بل سهلت . الثاني : بل زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It can mean that they embellished the claim that Benjamin stole, though he does not steal, while God has another purpose.
rows.anchor: زينت لكم أنفسكم أمرا في قولكم إن ابني سرق وهو لا يسرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob hopes God will bring all three brothers to him: Joseph, Benjamin, and the brother who stayed behind.
rows.anchor: يعني يوسف وأخيه المأخوذ في السرقة وأخيه المتخلف معه فهم ثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their situation and is wise in what He decrees about what they have described.
rows.anchor: العليم بأمركم , الحكيم في قضائه بما ذكرتم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: “Alas for Yusuf” means “what anguish,” as illustrated by a verse from Kathir.
rows.anchor: معناه واجزعاه قاله مجاهد , ومنه قول كثير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another gloss is “what grief,” with Hassan's elegy for the Prophet cited as usage.
rows.anchor: معناه يا جزعاه , قاله ابن عباس . قال حسان بن ثابت يرثي رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's exclamation may be a complaint to God seeking relief from his trial, not a complaint against God.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد به الشكوى إلى الله تعالى ولم يرد به الشكوى منه رغبا إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is a prayer, with the unspoken words “Lord, have mercy on my grief for Yusuf.”
rows.anchor: أنه أراد به الدعاء , وفيه قولان : أحدهما : مضمر وتقديره يا رب ارحم أسفي على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whiteness of Jacob's eyes may mean his vision weakened because of a white film from much weeping.
rows.anchor: ضعف بصره لبياض حصل فيه من كثرة بكائه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, his sight was completely lost.
rows.anchor: أنه ذهب بصره , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Kāẓim can mean inwardly stricken with grief.
rows.anchor: أنه الكمد , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: It can mean one who does not speak.
rows.anchor: أنه الذي لا يتكلم , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: It can mean subdued or overpowered.
rows.anchor: أنه المقهور , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: “You never cease mentioning Yusuf” means that Jacob keeps remembering him; a line by Aws ibn Hajar illustrates the idiom.
rows.anchor: معناه لا تزال تذكر يوسف , قال أوس بن حجر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another reading of tفتأ gives the sense of becoming weak or ceasing.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : تفتأ بمعنى تفتر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ḥaraḍ may mean worn-out with age.
rows.anchor: يعني هرما , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: It may mean gravely ill, in a condition just short of death.
rows.anchor: دنفا من المرض , وهو ما دون الموت , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that he would become unsound in mind.
rows.anchor: أنه الفاسد العقل , قاله محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of ḥaraḍ is bodily or mental corruption caused by illness or love; a line by al-ʿArjī illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحرض فساد الجسم والعقل من مرض أو عشق

rows.speaker: الجميع
rows.claim: “Or one of the dead” means that he would die like other dead people.
rows.anchor: يعني ميتا من الميتين قاله الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possibility is that God commanded Joseph to delay reunion as a test for a known benefit, since Joseph was a prophet under command.
rows.anchor: أن يكون فعل ذلك عن أمر الله تعالى , ابتلاء له لمصلحة علمها فيه لأنه نبي مأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that imprisonment made Joseph want to test his patience after being separated from his father.
rows.anchor: أنه بلي بالسجن , فأحب بعد فراقه أن يبلو نفسه بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have delayed to prepare gradually for joy, since sudden happiness carries risk.
rows.anchor: أن في مفاجأة السرور خطرا وأحب أن يروض نفسه بالتدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have waited so the greater king would not seem needy by summoning his family immediately after gaining power.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتصور الملك الأكبر فاقة أهله بتعجيل استدعائهم حين ملك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Bath means grief or worry.
rows.anchor: همي , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Bath may instead mean need or petition.
rows.anchor: حاجتي , حكاه ابن جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bath derives from spreading one's inward grief by expressing it; Jacob calls it his bath because he has disclosed it.
rows.anchor: والبث تفريق الهم بإظهار ما في النفس . وإنما شكا ما في نفسه فجعله بثا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Jacob knows that Joseph's dream is true and that his family will prostrate to him.
rows.anchor: أن رؤيا يوسف صادقة , وأني ساجد له , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi relates that Jacob sensed Joseph might be alive, asked the ruler, and said no truthful one exists on earth except a prophet.
rows.anchor: أحست نفسه حين أخبروه فدعا الملك وقال : لعله يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says a visitor asked Jacob why he looked as he did; he answered that time and many sorrows had caused it, then sought God's forgiveness after a divine rebuke.
rows.anchor: قال : طول الزمان وكثرة الأحزان . فأوحى الله إليه : يا يعقوب تشكوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥassasū means to search and investigate; the word is rooted in seeking something through the senses, and a line by ʿAdi ibn Zayd is cited.
rows.anchor: أي استعملوا وتعرفوا , ومنه قول عدي بن زيد

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Rūḥ of God can mean God's relief or deliverance.
rows.anchor: من فرج الله , قاله محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Another interpretation is God's mercy.
rows.anchor: من رحمة الله , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is associated with beneficial wind.
rows.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من الريح التي بالنفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob urged hope because the returned goods, Benjamin's detention, and the honor shown suggested that Joseph was near; a report also says he asked the Angel of Death whether he had taken Joseph's soul, and was told no.
rows.anchor: تنبه على يوسف برد البضاعة واحتباس أخيه وإظهار الكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' plea about hardship is an exceptionally gentle appeal that softens and stirs sympathy.
rows.anchor: وهذا من ألطف ترفيق وأبلغ استعطاف

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Their purpose in pleading was to have Benjamin returned to them.
rows.anchor: بأن يرد أخاهم عليهم , قاله ابن جرير

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Alternatively, they sought a full measure and favorable treatment.
rows.anchor: توفية كيلهم والمحاباة لهم , قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of mazjāh is pushing something along by driving it.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإزجاء السوق بالدفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by ʿAdi ibn al-Riqāʿ uses the verb تزجي as evidence for this root meaning.
rows.anchor: وفيه قول الشاعر عدي بن الرقاع . تزجي أغن كأن إبرة روقه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view says their merchandise consisted of dirhams.
rows.anchor: أنها كانت دراهم ، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عبدالله بن الحارث
rows.claim: Another says it was the wool and ghee of desert people.
rows.anchor: متاع الأعراب , صوف وسمن , قاله عبدالله بن الحارث

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: A third account identifies green grain and pine nuts.
rows.anchor: الحبة الخضراء وصنوبر , قاله أبو صالح

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: A fourth account says it was sawiq made from mukl.
rows.anchor: سويق المقل . قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A fifth account says it was a worn rope and sack.
rows.anchor: خلق الحبل والغرارة , وهو مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Mazjāh may mean poor-quality merchandise.
rows.anchor: أنها الرديئة , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: It may mean goods with little market demand.
rows.anchor: الكاسدة , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: It may mean a small quantity.
rows.anchor: القليلة , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains it as an amount too small to meet their need; he cites a line by al-Rāʿī.
rows.anchor: وهي التي لا تبلغ قدر الحاجة ومنه قول الراعي

rows.speaker: الراعي
rows.claim: A poetic line uses mazjāh for a need that is insufficient or of little value.
rows.anchor: ومرسل برسول غير متهم … وحاجة غير مزجاة من الحاج

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says mazjāh is a word from Persian.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : هي كلمة من لغة العجم

rows.speaker: الهيثمي
rows.claim: Al-Haythami instead says it is from Coptic.
rows.anchor: وقال الهيثمي : من لغة القبط

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: “Fulfill the measure” means the same measure Joseph had given to their brother.
rows.anchor: الكيل الذي كان قد كاله لأخيهم , وهو قول ابن جريج

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Alternatively, they ask for the same measure as before because their new merchandise was less valuable.
rows.anchor: مثل كيلهم الأول لأن بضاعتهم الثانية أقل , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي والحسن
rows.claim: “Give charity” can mean favor them by overlooking the difference between good and poor merchandise; this avoids asking prophets for prohibited charity.
rows.anchor: تفضل علينا بما بين الجياد والرديئة , قاله سعيد بن جبير والسدي والحسن

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: It may instead mean give them more than their due measure.
rows.anchor: تصدق علينا بالزيادة على حقنا , قاله سفيان بن عيينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says charity was prohibited only to Muhammad, not to all prophets.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : ولم تحرم الصدقة إلا على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وحده

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Another meaning is to give Benjamin back to them; the source also says one should not ask God for charity because charity seeks reward.
rows.anchor: تصدق علينا برد أخينا إلينا , قاله ابن جريج , وكره للرجل أن يقول في دعائه

rows.speaker: ابن شجرة وابن زيد
rows.claim: “Give charity” may mean pardon us or let us pass, as supported by a cited poem.
rows.anchor: معناه تجوز عنا , قاله ابن شجرة وابن زيد واستشهد بقول الشاعر

none: The segment contains only a broken opening brace.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers' admission that they were at fault refers to what they did to Joseph; it can mean either sinful or mistaken, with sinful implying culpability.
rows.anchor: أي فيما صنعوا بيوسف , وفيه قولان : أحدهما : آثمين . الثاني : مخطئين . والفرق بين الخاطئ والمخطئ أن الخاطئ آثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the brothers were young when they first acted, they became culpable by growing up and continuing to conceal what they had done.
rows.anchor: لما كبروا واستداموا إخفاء ما صنعوا صاروا حينئذ خاطئين

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: “No reproach on you” can mean no blame or alteration is laid on them.
rows.anchor: لا تغيير عليكم , وهو قول سفيان ابن عيينة

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: It can mean no reproach for what they did.
rows.anchor: لا تأنيب فيما صنعتم , قاله ابن إسحاق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: It may mean Joseph has no aversion to what they said.
rows.anchor: لا إباء عليكم في قولكم , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth gloss is that there will be no punishment.
rows.anchor: لا عقاب عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forgiveness may follow their repentance, confession, and regret.
rows.anchor: لتوبتهم بالاعتراف والندم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God forgives because Joseph has made pardon permissible for them.
rows.anchor: لإحلاله لهم بالعفو عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is the most merciful” may refer to God's making Joseph a king.
rows.anchor: في صنعه بي حين جعلني ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to God's mercy in pardoning the brothers' earlier offense.
rows.anchor: في عفوه عنكم عما تقدم من ذنبكم

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic example uses fand for foolishness.
rows.anchor: قم في البرية فا جددها عن الفند أي عن السفه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والضحاك
rows.claim: “Unless you accuse me of lying” is one interpretation; a poetic line uses fand to mean a lie.
rows.anchor: لولا أن تكذبون , قاله سعيد بن جبير والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Another meaning is “unless you weaken me”; tafnīd means weakening someone's judgment, as a cited poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: لولا أن تضعفون , قاله ابن إسحاق . والتفنيد : تضعيف الرأي

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: A further interpretation is “unless you blame me,” supported by a line by Jarir.
rows.anchor: لولا أن تلوموني , قاله ابن بحر . ومنه قول جرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's statement was directed to his grandsons because his sons were absent, which shows that a grandfather has the status of a father.
rows.anchor: وكان قول هذا لأولاد بنيه , لغيبة بنيه عنه , فدل هذا على أن الجد أب

rows.speaker: أبو الهذيل
rows.claim: One report says Jacob detected Joseph's scent from ten days' travel away.
rows.anchor: أنه وجدها من مسافة عشرة أيام . قاله أبو الهذيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another says the scent was detected from eight days' travel away.
rows.anchor: من مسيرة ثمانية أيام , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A third report says the distance was six days' travel.
rows.anchor: من مسيرة ستة أيام , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Jacob was in Canaan and Joseph in Egypt, a distance of eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: وكان يعقوب بأرض كنعان ويوسف بمصر وبينهما ثمانون فرسخا , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: The brothers' phrase means that Jacob remains in his old error.
rows.anchor: أي في خطئك القديم , قاله ابن عباس وابن زيد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: It may instead accuse Jacob of long-standing madness.
rows.anchor: في جنونك القديم , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة وسفيان
rows.claim: Another view is that they meant his old love for Joseph.
rows.anchor: في محبتك القديمة , قاله قتادة وسفيان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: A fourth view is that they meant Jacob's old misery, with Labid's line illustrating the sense of ḍalāl.
rows.anchor: في شقائك القديم , قاله مقاتل , ومنه قول لبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers may be Jacob's sons, who did not intend insult and therefore were not sinful, or his young grandsons.
rows.anchor: بنوه , ولم يقصدوا بذلك ذما فيأثموا . والثاني : بنو نبيه وكانوا صغارا
